meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I'm listening, Hale. It's 4:15 and I have a call at 4:40. Why does my son have a zero?
I don't have time for this. The zero stands.
"The zero stands." On what basis, Hale? Nobody called me before it went in, and Owen found out from his phone in the middle of class.
Sorry. That came out wrong. Let me show you what I actually have: the essay quotes a line that isn't in Hamlet, and his October 15 outline argued cowardice, which the essay never mentions.
Okay. Students change their argument between an outline and an essay, Hale, and a misremembered quote is not a zero. Which line, and show me the outline with its date on it.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still want the zero withdrawn, an apology for how Owen found out, and a written promise that nothing goes on his record. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She stayed at her opening position, with nothing agreed, and she still wants the zero withdrawn, an apology and a promise in writing that nothing goes on his record; the fair outcome is a private supervised rewrite with nothing on file under procedure 4.4, and the meeting never reached it, though her time had not run out.
What moved her: You apologized for how you started and then gave her something specific, a line that is not in Hamlet and an outline from October 15 that argued something the essay never does, which earned a flat okay and a request to see both.
What cost ground: Opening with the zero stands and no time for this gave her the process failure to attack first, since nobody called her before the mark went in, and you never answered that.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your evidence pointed at the outline and the essay's content, not at any late night, so it was nowhere near that night, and it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fights so hard.
Try next time: Right after the apology, say in one sentence that the zero went in before you called her, then put the exact line and the dated outline in front of her so she can check them herself.
